summary: Standing 100-ft steel Moon Tower on State Game Lands 211, Dauphin County; NHLR dates it 1922, while other sources give 1923 for an older tower and 1967 for the standing one.

facts.design: Steel tower with a wrap-around catwalk, unusual for Pennsylvania; Willhite identifies the standing structure as a Caldwell Model Tower.

access.note: On State Game Lands No. 211; reached on foot from a game land gate on Ellendale Road. The Stony Valley history site says climbing is not advisable.

visit.trail_note: Park at the pulloff by the game land gate and walk about two miles up Rattling Run Road / Horse-Shoe Trail, then about 0.5 miles to the tower. NHLR describes a four-hour hike and Stony Valley gives distances; the two measure the walk differently.

events.note: NHLR gives 1922 for the standing lookout, built by the Philadelphia & Reading Coal & Iron Company as a 100-foot steel tower.
A 60-foot Blaw-Knox tower built by company fire wardens at the original site, about 2 miles northeast along the Appalachian Trail.
FFLOS says the Blaw-Knox tower was replaced in 1967; Willhite says the present Caldwell tower was built in 1967 further down the ridge.
Listed on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register as US 498, the former tower site.
Listed on NHLR as US 1262, registered January 15, 2018.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates the standing tower to 1922. FFLOS and Willhite date a 1923 Blaw-Knox tower to the original site and a 1967 tower to the standing one. The story reports both and does not choose.
NHLR gives 100 ft (30.5 m); Willhite gives 82 ft and notes other sources say 100 ft. The record keeps 30.5 m.
NHLR describes a four-hour hike; Stony Valley describes about 2.5 miles of walking from the gate. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 1922 build year comes from NHLR alone; the other two sources put the 1923 tower on the old site and the 1967 tower on the standing site, so the build date is contested. The FFLOS entry (US 498) is for the former site, not the standing lookout, so it is not a second record of the same tower. No staffing or fire history was found for the standing tower, so no staffing facts or fire events are recorded. Stony Valley gives the dismantling only as by the 1970s, so no removal event is recorded. Height conflicts (100 ft vs 82 ft). No new photos added.
